# Slang Should Be Contextual Slang terms and in particular netspeak should only be used if they make sense for the character and the context. You should think carefully about whether use of a modern day slang term enhances or detracts from immersion for you and your fellow players before applying it.
## Slang [bold]Themed slang is encouraged[/bold]. Using terms like "spacer", "bloodred", "mats", and other terms which have become common and universal SS14 shorthand are a core part of the world and culture and may be used freely. Likewise, there is no issue with terms like "spacing" and "tritfire" or shorthands like "sec", "med", "cap" or "salv".
Certain terms like "shitsec", "nukie", and "tider" remain significantly discouraged due to their low roleplay nature and general lack of logical presence in the world. You may freely reference things like the culture of tiding and the nukie films, but the terms should not be applied as practical shorthands.
You may freely invent slang for your characters to use, so long as they are not used in ways that violate server rules. Creation and usage of personalized slang or fictitious cultural terms is commendable and very much in the spirit of SpL.
## Pop Culture And Netspeak [bold]Netspeak is heavily discouraged[/bold]. This includes terms like "based", "larp", "peak", and "goated". Use is permitted in moderation, but you should have good IC justification for using terms that are half a millennia outdated. Be creative with your words instead!
[bold]References to modern pop culture must be contextual[/bold]. You should not randomly blurt out "among us" or "six seven", but you may reference films or meme images as "ancient classics" or similar such sentiments. If you must reference something from the modern age, try to make it make sense from the perspective of someone 500 years into the future.
## Acronyms. [bold]Acronyms are not permitted[/bold]. This includes phrases like "lol", "ik", "idc", "tf", and other common modern-world text based shorthands.
Normally, SS14 has a chat sanitizer in place to automatically filter such terms out. It has been massively scaled back in SpL to allow innocuous uses of the base noises (such as "mf" being used as a muffled noise or a stuttering character happening to say "gl" when pronouncing glue). This is not a free pass to use them in lieu of actual words.
